result.title: Diagnosis is not a policy: a state-transition audit of caoability-conditioned test-time inference
result.summary: Test-time actions can satisfy retrieval, state-realization, program-consistency, or rendering objectives without correcting an answer. Test-time Error Response and Realizability Audit (TERRA) is an evaluation/auditing protocol, not a new inference algorithm. It uses a unified decomposition of intervention outcomes into applicability, target-state realization, endpoint translation, harm, and resource/inference cost. Paired comparisons fix the incoming state and evaluation conditions; cross-model analyses vary the receiving configuration. Executable financial reasoning experiments yield three findings: the same context expansion can harm one configuration and benefit another; sufficient evidence does not ensure correctness because configurations differ in evidence-to-answer translation; and diagnostic headroom---accuracy attainable with idealized diagnostic information over the measured baseline---plus local consistency does not ensure practical gains. Action value is $V(a\mid x,m)$, not diagnosis alone; diagnosis is not a deployable policy $π(a\mid x,m)$.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TERRA 审计协议，把 test-time 干预结果分解为适用性、目标状态实现、端点翻译、危害与推理成本，并通过固定输入状态的配对比较与跨模型比较，在可执行金融推理任务上说明诊断能带来的准确率上限并不等于可部署的收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态是否实现」与「证据到答案翻译」的分离及成本记账，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 干预是否真正改写答案、THINK/LOOK 收益来自何处；但实验为文本金融推理，能否迁移到多模态与视觉证据筛选仍需阅读正文确认。
